hints.title: Start at Index K
hints.text: Initialize a window with left = k and right = k, with minimum element min_val = nums[k].

hints.title: Expand Toward Larger Neighbor
hints.text: At each expansion step, extend toward the side having the larger adjacent value to maintain highest possible min_val.

hints.title: Track Maximum Score
hints.text: Update min_val = min(min_val, new_element) and evaluate score = min_val * (right - left + 1) until entire array is covered.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maximumScore(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        l, r = k, k
        min_val = nums[k]
        ans = min_val

        while l > 0 or r < n - 1:
            left_val = nums[l - 1] if l > 0 else -1
            right_val = nums[r + 1] if r < n - 1 else -1
            if left_val >= right_val:
                l -= 1
                min_val = min(min_val, nums[l])
            else:
                r += 1
                min_val = min(min_val, nums[r])
            ans = max(ans, min_val * (r - l + 1))

        return ans
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating all valid subarrays around k takes O(n^2) quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Greedy two-pointer window expansion covers all potential optimal boundaries in linear O(n) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate proves that expanding toward the strictly larger neighboring element never misses the optimum.
